items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I think that’s why Artie Shaw got out of the business. Because how many times can I play that chorus on “Stardust” and mean it?

ctx.x: I’ve always wondered sometimes, those solos from the Miller recordings, if they were improvised at the time. Because they became like THE solo to play. They actually would write them out, they were written out in the arrangements.

I suppose later on they were, but I think at the time, when they knew they were going to make a record of a particular tune, and they had a solo, they would work out a solo, play it on the record, and maybe play it from then on, which I don’t think is all that bad really. I mean if it was good enough to play on the record, why not play it a few times more? I mean I don’t think it would be good to do it year on end, in fact I think that’s why Artie Shaw got out of the business. Because how many times can I play…
Bobby Hackett — didn’t he play that beautiful solo on “String of Pearls” was it?
